name: Storage quotas and eviction
plain: How much each site may store on the device, per browser.
meaning: Caps how much a site can keep (IndexedDB, Cache, files). Large quotas let a site store gigabytes; quota values are derived from total disk size, so estimate() was padded to limit fingerprinting.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt; browser enforces quota and throws QuotaExceededError.
access.iframe: Cross-origin frames get a fraction (Safari about 10% of the parent's)
steps: Browser compares against the origin quota
Under disk pressure unprotected origins are evicted least recently used, all or nothing

fields.name: Chrome and Edge
fields.range: up to 60% per origin; about 80% across the browser

fields.name: Firefox best effort
fields.range: min(10% of disk, 10 GiB) per origin; 10 GiB per eTLD+1 group

fields.name: Safari 14+ and iOS 17+
fields.range: about 60% per origin; 80% total; embedded WebViews 15% and 20%

fields.name: Chrome opaque response padding
fields.range: about 7 MB per opaque cross-origin response

limits.headline: Can store only what your browser allows, and may lose it when space is low
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Check roughly how much space it has used and may use
Store data up to its limit
Get an error when the limit is reached
cannot: Go over its limit, which varies by browser and free disk
Stop the browser clearing it when space is low, unless storage is protected
See your exact free disk space, since the numbers are rough
limits.differs: Limits differ by browser. Chrome, Firefox and Safari each set their own caps.

story.what_it_is: How much each site may store on your device, which differs by browser.

marketing.name: Storage for the web
marketing.pitch: Google explains how much a site can store and how browsers manage quota and cleanup.

marketing.name: Updates to storage policy
marketing.pitch: Apple explains the new Safari limits on how much a site can store.

story.for_you: You never see the limit, until a site runs out of room. Then it may stop saving, ask you to free space or lose offline data.
story.for_makers: Makers plan their offline features around the limit. A big game or editor needs lots of space. The quota number and the way it behaves can also help tell browsers and private modes apart.

use_cases.example: A browser game with large levels checks the quota first, then downloads only what fits.
A podcast or music web app tells you how many songs it can keep offline.
A web video editor warns you before a project grows beyond the space it can store.
A web email app keeps the last month of mail offline, as much as the quota allows.
A fraud service notes a tiny quota, which can mean private mode or an emulator.
A site team measures typical quotas to design offline features.
A fingerprint script reads the exact quota number as one more clue about your device and disk.

technical_bounds: Quota computed from total disk, not free space
Safari deletes script-written data after 7 days without interaction (ITP)
Eviction is LRU and all or nothing per origin

history.change: Per-origin quota raised to about 60% of disk
Eviction policy moved to origin groups
